title: Google Images search reproducibly causes tab crash
body: I'm using Firefox 115.0b7 compiled from source on Debian GNU/Linux 10 with a fresh profile and no add-ons. Every Google Images search reproducibly crashes the tab: results appear very briefly and are replaced by “Gah. Your tab just crashed.” stderr says the content process exited on signal 11, and I included the corresponding crash-report URL. Please advise what else I can do to diagnose this.

symptoms_visible: Every Google Images results page briefly displays images and is then replaced by “Gah. Your tab just crashed.”
When it crashes, stderr says the content process exited on signal 11.
N0.label: N0 reproducible Google Images tab crash reported

symptoms_visible: Google Images crashes the tab in official stable, beta, Nightly, and an older Firefox build, including with fresh profiles and troubleshooting mode.
The crash occurs on my Debian 10 machine but not on a near-identical Debian 11 machine.
N1.label: N1 browser regression and profile causes excluded

symptoms_visible: Google Images still crashes the tab on the affected Linux system.
N2.label: N2 old-kernel JIT stack-probe diagnosis established

symptoms_visible: Opening the provided standalone browser test also crashes the tab on the affected system.
N3.label: N3 crash reproduced independently of Google

symptoms_visible: With the provided standalone test, build 1 displays “ok” without crashing, while build 2 crashes the tab.
N4.label: N4 candidate build differential confirmed

symptoms_visible: As a separate tester, I reproduced the Google Images tab crash with Firefox 114.0.2 on Debian 10 and Debian 9 virtual machines; on those same systems I can no longer reproduce it with Firefox 115.0, the 2023-06-26 Nightly, or the 102.13esr test build.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix shipped and independently verified, original reporter not retested

question_patterns: Does it still crash in troubleshooting mode and with an official Mozilla build?
Can you test stable, beta, or Nightly with a fresh profile and report whether they behave differently?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I get the same crash in troubleshooting mode and with official Mozilla builds: stable 114.0.2, Developer Edition 115.0b8, and Nightly 116.0a1. I used completely new profiles and shared crash reports from the tests.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The official Mozilla build works normally; only my locally compiled build crashes.
The same versions and modes crash, but the Nightly build ID is from the following day.

question_patterns: Does an older Firefox version reproduce the crash?
Can you retry a Firefox build that previously displayed Google Images correctly?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Firefox 111.0.1 also crashes now, even though I know I previously used that version for Google Images without a problem.

question_patterns: Can you compare the result on another Linux installation or machine?
Does the crash reproduce on a newer Debian system?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On near-identical machines it occurs on Debian 10 Buster but not on Debian 11 Bullseye.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It also crashes identically on Debian 11 and on a current Linux kernel.

edges.comment: Reporter-only evidence from c1-c8: the original reporter tested safe mode, official and custom builds, versions 111 through 116, fresh profiles, and near-identical Debian 10/11 systems. The EnterBaseline/Interpreter stack observation was separately volunteered by the reporter in c6 and is added to N1.volunteered_info.

solution.intent: Diagnose the crash as Firefox JIT stack probing that attempts a very large OSR stack frame without moving RSP, conflicting with the stack-growth rules of older Linux kernels.
solution.concrete_example: Google's image-search script creates an OSR frame larger than 150 KB. Firefox probes pages in that frame while RSP remains at its old value, but older x86 Linux kernels reject stack accesses more than roughly 64 KB away from RSP, causing the content-process segfault.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied crash reports, cross-version behavior, the Debian 10/11 contrast, and a stack containing EnterBaselineInterpreterAtBranch. Engineers derived the precise mechanism from crash memory maps, disassembly, kernel behavior, and JIT code analysis in c14, c19, c23, c29, and c37-c43. The user did not identify the 64 KB kernel rule or the missing RSP adjustment.

edges.comment: Engineer-side analysis from c14, c19, c23, c27, c29, and c33-c43. No participant setup is merged into the reporter's machine here: the new facts are explicitly engineer inferences from the collected crash evidence.

question_patterns: Please open this provided standalone browser test and tell me exactly what happens.
Can you run the attached browser test on an affected machine and report whether the tab completes or crashes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I opened the standalone test on my affected Debian 10 system, and the tab crashes there too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The standalone test completes normally on the same system where Google Images crashes.
The standalone test crashes on another affected older-Linux machine as well.

edges.comment: Measurement from c48-c51. The browser test was created by participant12 and run by multiple affected participants, including Debian 10 users; those affected users are folded into the simulated user side for this raw crash result. The test's intended JIT mechanism remains engineer knowledge from e2, not part of the question or user answer.

question_patterns: Please run the same standalone test in each of these two Linux builds and report the result for build 1 and build 2.
Can you compare the two provided builds with the browser test and tell me exactly what each one displays?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Build 1 runs the JavaScript test and says “ok” without crashing. Build 2 crashes the tab.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both provided builds crash the tab with the same test.
Build 1 says “ok” and build 2 crashes on my Slackware machine as well.

edges.comment: Pre-landing candidate-build measurement from c52-c62. Affected participants on Debian, Slackware, and other older-kernel systems are folded into one user side. One participant initially reported both builds crashing because another Firefox instance was reused, then reran correctly and confirmed build 1 worked; the raw consensus result is build 1 “ok,” build 2 crash.

solution.intent: Change the Linux JIT stack-probing loop to use the stack pointer register while probing, so each probe remains within the distance older kernels permit, then provide a Firefox build containing that change and ask the affected user to verify it.
solution.concrete_example: Temporarily advance RSP as the JIT probes the large stack frame instead of probing more than about 64 KB away from an unchanged stack pointer. Install a Firefox build containing this change and retest Google Images and the standalone browser test.

edges.comment: Implementation and landing from c43-c44 and c55-c59. Post-landing verification is not modeled as an upstream clarification: c73 is terminal-side evidence from a separate tester who first reproduced on Debian 10 and Debian 9, then could not reproduce in builds containing the landed change. The original reporter never posted a final retest, so user_perceives_resolved remains false.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: a Google Images script created a very large JIT OSR stack frame, and Firefox probed that frame without updating RSP; older Linux kernels reject stack accesses more than roughly 64 KB from the current stack pointer, causing the content-process segfault.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the cross-version and cross-system evidence, the standalone reproducer, and the two-build differential rather than inferred from the Google Images symptom alone.
The technical fix must use the stack pointer register while performing the stack probes so the probes remain compatible with older Linux kernel stack-growth rules.

Must not attribute the crash to the reporter's custom build, profile, add-ons, troubleshooting-mode settings, or the process_util_posix.cc warning; those directions are contradicted by the collected evidence, and that warning only reports that another process crashed.
Must not treat Google's temporary page change as a complete browser-side resolution because the standalone test still reproduces the Firefox crash independently of Google.

Must ask the original reporter to verify Google Images or the standalone test on a Firefox build containing the fix before declaring the reporter's own system resolved; the thread only contains final fixed-build confirmation from a separate tester.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical Linux user who compiles Firefox from source, tests multiple official builds and profiles, reads native crash stacks, and can compare behavior across operating-system installations, but defers to JavaScript-engine specialists for the precise JIT and kernel mechanism.
persona_hint.communication_style: Methodical, detailed, and proactive; supplies exact versions and crash-report links, runs additional tests without prompting, clearly labels tentative conclusions, and asks what evidence would help triage.
